title: Adversarial Manipulation of Safety Concept Vectors

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling chain: if concept vector-based safety can be bypassed by adversarial inputs crafted to be orthogonal to known vectors, this directly undermines a proposed safety mechanism. Characterizing this attack surface is essential before deployment and has immediate implications for defense design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: White-box adversarial optimization over activations requires gradient-based attacks through the model, which is technically demanding for beginners. Understanding activation geometry, implementing orthogonality constraints, and debugging optimization loops are advanced tasks. Medium compute may be tight for iterative optimization on 8B models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one attack type (orthogonal crafting) against one vector (toxicity), but implementing the attack, measuring success rate, and testing probe monitoring adds multiple experiment dimensions. Could be scoped to a small model but still requires building the attack pipeline.
